## What Is Algorithmic Trading  
Algorithmic trading, often called algo trading, uses computer programs to execute trades based on predefined rules. Those rules can be as simple as “buy when the 50‑day moving average crosses above the 200‑day moving average” or as complex as machine‑learning models that ingest news sentiment, order‑book data, and alternative data streams. The main appeal is speed and consistency—computers can react to market moves in milliseconds, removing the emotional bias that often trips up human traders.

For newcomers, the concept can feel intimidating, but the barrier to entry has dropped dramatically. Modern platforms provide visual strategy builders, drag‑and‑drop interfaces, and extensive libraries of pre‑coded indicators. This means you don’t need a PhD in computer science to start experimenting; you just need a clear idea of what you want the algorithm to do and a willingness to test it rigorously.

## Why Use Algorithmic Trading Software  
### Save Time and Reduce Emotion  
Manual trading demands constant screen‑watching, quick calculations, and disciplined execution. Algorithmic software handles the repetitive tasks, freeing you to focus on research, risk management, or simply enjoying life outside the markets. Because trades follow a strict rule set, fear and greed have less room to interfere.

### Backtest Before You Risk Capital  
One of the biggest advantages is the ability to test a strategy on historical data before putting real money on the line. Good software lets you simulate months or years of trading in seconds, showing you metrics like win rate, average profit per trade, maximum drawdown, and Sharpe ratio. This iterative process helps you refine rules and avoid costly mistakes.
